script.title: Labour Variances: rate, efficiency, idle time
script.caption_hook: Labour cost went up: did you pay more, or work slow?

lines.say: Ma'am, labour cost went up. Was it the pay or slow work?
Labour variance is the cost gap, split into rate, efficiency and idle time. Say 100 units, four hours each, ₹50 per hour.
Okay, but how big is the total gap?
Standard is 400 hours at ₹50, so ₹20,000. Actual is 450 hours at ₹52, so ₹23,400.
Rate first, on hours paid. 450 hours times fifty minus fifty-two gives ₹900 adverse.

board.title: Rate Variance
board.sub: AH paid: hours paid. SR/AR: std/actual rate

lines.say: And slow work is efficiency, right?
Yes, on hours worked. 30 hours were idle, so worked is 420. Fifty times 400 minus 420 is ₹1,000 adverse.

board.title: Efficiency Var.
board.sub: SH: std hours. AH worked = paid − idle

lines.say: Paid but no output. Fifty times 30 is ₹1,500, always adverse.

board.title: Idle Time Variance
board.sub: Idle hours × standard rate; always Adverse

lines.say: Do all three add up to the total?
Yes! 900 plus 1,000 plus 1,500 is ₹3,400 adverse. It matches the total.
Got it! Rate is price, the others are hours.
Remember: rate is price per hour, while efficiency and idle are hours used.

check_notes: Writer: Worked example: SH=100×4=400, SR ₹50, AH paid 450, idle 30, worked 420, AR ₹52. LCV=20,000−23,400=−3,400 A; LRV=−900; LEV=−1,000; Idle=−1,500; sum −3,400. Assumes standard 4 hrs/unit and actual output 100 units.

Checker: Line 14 (voice and board 'Hours = use'): calling idle time 'hours used' is misleading, because idle hours are paid but not worked. Better: 'Rate is price per hour; efficiency is hours worked versus standard; idle time is hours paid but not worked.'
Checker: Line 4: the script never says the 450 hours are hours paid, which the rate and idle split depend on. Better: 'Actual is 450 hours paid at ₹52, so ₹23,400.'
